Building of the Oakleaf library

The Oakleaf library is distributed in the form of the source code, and must be compiled prior to use.

It is also pre-packaged in GNU/Debian and Ubuntu. The install is, by the way: 

    # [sudo] apt install liboakleaf1 liboakleaf-dev liboakleaf-doc

Prerequisites

A modern Fortran 2008+ compiler and Minpack are required. Minpack should be installed in the development version, the package is minpack-dev.

Getting sources

Download the source archive, and unpack it: 

    $ wget https://integral.physics.muni.cz/pub/oakleaf/oakleaf-2.0.0.tar.gz
    $ tar zxf oakleaf-2.0.0.tar.gz

The package build

The Oakleaf library should to be build in the following steps: 

    $ cd oakleaf-2.0.0/
    $ ./configure FCFLAGS="-O2 -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow"
    $ make
    # make install    # as root, or sudo

It can be later un-installed, if the build directory still exists, by command 

    $ cd [some directory]/oakleaf-2.0.0/
    # make uninstall    # as root

The building can be customised via optional parameters of the configure. The optimisation by the parameter "-O2" is reccomended, as well as "-ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow" which reports serious numerical problems and omits irrelevant ones. The library is installed under /usr/local by default (see configure --help).

If Minpack is not found, although installed, by ./configure, try to add LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib" (adjust the path) and check presence of libminpack.a.

Smoke tests

The Oakleaf package has included a verification. Basic tests can be executed as: 

    $ make check

The advanced testing, under a high voltage, is performed by 

    $ VOLTAGE=high make check

The placement

By default, the library is placed under /usr/local according to the switch --prefix= of ./configure. A program is compiled as 

    gfortran -I/usr/local/include ... -L/usr/local/lib -loakleaf

If the library is installed by a packaging system, --prefix=/usr is used. For GNU/Debian, as well as derivatives like Ubuntu or Mint, compilation requires -I/usr/include, but -L/usr/lib can be omited: 

    gfortran -I/usr/include ... -loakleaf

The library can be found in /usr/lib/<arch>, where the arch x86_64-linux-gnu is just an example.
